name: TextBox 1001
text:
Kumbh Mela: The World's Largest Human Gathering
Kumbh Mela at Nashik–Trimbakeshwar draws crores of pilgrims across a few weeks — the single largest peaceful gathering of people on Earth.
Organising and managing an event of this scale depends on fast, accurate communication — about routes, timings, crowd levels and emergencies — reaching millions of people at once.
Where Social Media Fits In
Social media — X, WhatsApp, Instagram, YouTube — has become the de-facto communication backbone of kumbh Mela: officials broadcast advisories, pilgrims track family members, and crowd conditions are reported in real time by attendees themselves.
This project studies that role in depth and proposes KumbhRakshak, a Social Intelligence Hub that makes social media a reliable tool for organising and managing the event — not just a source of noise.

name: TextBox 1002
text:
The Core Problem
Social media accelerates how kumbh Mela is organised and managed — but the same openness lets unverified claims travel just as fast as verified ones.
A single false post (“stampede at Gate 7”, “route closed”) can move thousands of pilgrims within minutes, long before any authority can confirm or deny it.
Existing WhatsApp/X coordination is manual and slow: officials post updates by hand, duplicate reports flood in from the same incident, and there is no automatic way to check a viral claim against ground reality.
Problem Statement
How can social media be used to organise and manage kumbh Mela crowds effectively, while verifying claims fast enough to prevent misinformation-driven panic?

name: TextBox 1003
text:
Primary Objective
Turn social media from a source of chaos into a reliable command tool for organising and managing kumbh Mela — verify claims fast, coordinate response, and push accurate information back to pilgrims and families.
Specific Objectives
Ingest and monitor viral posts from X, WhatsApp and Instagram in real time.
Verify urgent social claims against ground-camera evidence before acting on them.
Cluster duplicate reports so one real incident is not logged hundreds of times.
Push verified advisories back onto the same social channels pilgrims already trust.
Keep families connected to pilgrim safety status even when mobile networks are congested.

name: TextBox 1005
text:
What the Literature Confirms
Social media genuinely helps organise mega gatherings — sharing schedules, safety advice and building participation (Aishwarya & Vinay 2025; Tiwari & Chowdhary 2022).
Researchers already mine social posts (e.g. Twitter analytics) to understand crowd mood and experience in real time (Kumbh Twitter Study, 2020).
The same channels — X, Facebook, WhatsApp — are consistently identified as the primary vectors for disaster misinformation, which spreads faster when official information is delayed (JMIR, 2025; Simon et al., 2016).
The Gap We Address
No reviewed study combines social-media listening with automated, ground-truth (camera-based) verification and a feedback loop back onto the same platforms — this is exactly what KumbhRakshak's Social Intelligence Hub is built to do.

name: TextBox 1012
text:
Data Flow
Camera feeds and live social posts are ingested in parallel; NLP and vision models extract claims and events.
Claims are cross-checked against ground-camera evidence; duplicate reports are clustered into one incident.
A risk score is computed; a human commander confirms before any alert or advisory is issued.
Verified information flows back out through the dashboard and onto WhatsApp/social channels.

name: TextBox 1013
text:
Key Implemented Modules
Social Ingestion Adapter — pulls posts from mock/official feeds and normalises them for processing.
Social NLP Engine — extracts the claim, location and urgency from free-text captions and transcripts.
Embedding & Similarity Engine (sentence-transformers) — clusters near-duplicate posts about the same incident.
Verification Engine — compares a claim's evidence against camera-based ground truth and returns VERIFIED / UNVERIFIED / CONTRADICTED.
Risk Scoring Engine — a transparent, explainable formula combining confidence, severity and spread.
Command Dashboard (Next.js) — live map, KPIs, incident feed and the “Verify This Reel” claim-checking tool.
Tech Stack in Practice
FastAPI backend + Firebase Firestore, WebSocket broadcast for real-time updates, Docker Compose for packaging.

name: TextBox 1001
text:
Demonstrated Outcomes (Prototype)
Successfully clusters dozens of duplicate social posts about the same incident into a single tracked report.
“Verify This Reel” correctly returns UNVERIFIED for a simulated false stampede claim, citing the absence of supporting camera evidence.
Command dashboard displays live KPIs, map markers and social-report volume during a simulated Major Snan event.
Recycled/old video clips are flagged via perceptual-hash matching before they can be mistaken for live footage.
End-to-end flow — social post → clustering → verification → dashboard alert — runs within seconds in the demo environment.
Scope of Current Results
Results are from the simulated/demo environment (mock social adapter, simulated cameras); field validation is the next step.

name: TextBox 1002
text:
Prioritised Roadmap
Platform partnerships: direct API ties with X, Meta and YouTube for faster verification and takedown signals.
Two-way pilgrim channel: let verified users report incidents directly into the system, not just be monitored.
Predictive rumour modelling: forecast which claims are likely to go viral before they peak.
Trusted-source registry and a rumour heatmap showing where false claims are clustering geographically.
Multilingual social assistant replying in Hindi, Marathi and English across WhatsApp and X.
Public service extensions: accessibility support and social-media-based lost-and-found alerts.
